title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 105-106
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 105 to 106 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'यज्ञभृद्यज्ञकृद्यज्ञी यज्ञभुग्यज्ञसाधनः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 105 to 106 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 105 to 106.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 105 to 106** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **यज्ञभृद्यज्ञकृद्यज्ञी यज्ञभुग्यज्ञसाधनः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**यज्ञभृद्यज्ञकृद्यज्ञी यज्ञभुग्यज्ञसाधनः । यज्ञान्तकृद्यज्ञगुह्यमन्नमन्नाद एव च ॥** **आत्मयोनिः स्वयंजातो वैखानः सामगायनः । देवकीनन्दनः स्रष्टा क्षितीशः पापनाशनः ॥**

He carries the sacrifice, performs it and is its very form. The one who enjoys its fruit and the means of it is that God of gods. He completes the sacrifice, he is its secret, he is food and he is the eater of food. Born of himself, arisen by his own will, Vaikhana, who sings the Sama is he. The son of Devaki, the creator, lord of the earth and destroyer of sin, is that God of gods.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 105 to 106 mean?
faq.a: He carries the sacrifice, performs it and is its very form. The one who enjoys its fruit and the means of it is that God of gods. He completes the sacrifice, he is its secret, he is food and he is the eater of food. Born of himself, arisen by his own will, Vaikhana, who sings the Sama is he. The son of Devaki, the creator, lord of the earth and destroyer of sin, is that God of gods.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
